advances: An integer-width necessity for a single common minimum with one-sided positive supporting coarea. No affine outer envelope, menu construction or mixed-depth payment is used.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Use the proper and supporting coareas of fact 74db6b5e20b3444a, with the common divisor equal to the continuous normal length. If two outside supports were at $L_1<L_2<a$, interpolation between a plane point in the first and a strictly captured point at $a$ gives a strictly captured point in the second. This is impossible. The same argument applies on the right. Changing the sign of the margin interchanges inside and outside support while preserving properness, giving the inside assertion. An outside-supporting base on the left is the smallest projected base of the closed cut body: if a lower base had a point in the cut body, its interpolation with a strictly captured point at $a$ would be strictly captured at the supporting base. The right endpoint and the opposite cut body follow by the same interpolation with the reversed base or margin.

The hypotheses of fact 74db6b5e20b3444a hold for these two marks and their common original physical cap. Its left side is positive by properness and $m>0$, so the cap has outside coarea at some $L<a$. By uniqueness the left-side coarea lies at $L$ and its value $A$ is positive. The quota gives
$$
m\sum_{z\ {\rm proper}}S_z\le A(h-m)
$$
after dropping the inside penalty. For $L<z<b$ interpolate a boundary point at $L$ with a strictly captured point at $b$ to obtain a strictly captured point at $z$. A strictly missed point at $L$ and one at $b$ give a strictly missed point at $z$. The fiber at $z$ is full-dimensional, since it contains the interpolation of the two positive endpoint fibers. Thus every integer $L+1,\ldots,b$ is proper.

For $d\ge2$, interpolate the whole plane section at $L$ with a plane point at $b$. In the parallel continuous cutting planes this gives a translated $(b-z)/h$ dilation of the section at $L$ inside the section at $z$. Hence $S_z\ge A((b-z)/h)^{d-1}$ for $L<z<b$, including the common coarea divisor. Summing the resulting $h-1$ bounds gives the displayed finite sum inequality. Strict increase of $t^{d-1}$ on $[0,\infty)$ and strict Bernoulli give
$$
\sum_{j=1}^{h-1}(j/h)^{d-1}>\int_0^{h-1}(t/h)^{d-1}\,dt
=\frac{h}{d}(1-1/h)^d>\frac{h}{d}-1.
$$
If $m\ge d$, multiplication by $m$ contradicts the upper bound $h-m$. For $d=1$, every proper section and the supporting endpoint at $L$ have coarea $A=1/\|u\|$, where $u$ is the cap's continuous normal. The $h$ proper integer fibers $L+1,\ldots,b$ give $mhA\le A(h-m)$, impossible for an integer $m\ge1$. The right-sided case uses $z\mapsto-z$, which preserves all sampled measures and local tilt hypotheses.

statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, and sum the $d$-volumes of its integer fibers. Let a nonvertical closed cap be proper in the fibers at integers $a<b$ and locally minimize cap mass at each of two marks on those bases under pure base tilt, with the respective buffer offsets and the continuous normal fixed. Suppose all positive outside-supporting coarea strictly beyond $[a,b]$ lies to its left. Then there is a unique outside-supporting positive fiber on the left, at an integer $L<a$ with positive coarea. Put $m=b-a$ and $h=b-L$. If $d\ge2$, then
$$
m\sum_{j=1}^{h-1}(j/h)^{d-1}\le h-m,\qquad m\le d-1.
$$
If $d=1$, these hypotheses are impossible. Reversing the base gives the same width conclusion when all positive outside coarea beyond the source interval lies to its right.

Independently of minimality, if a cap is proper at both $a$ and $b$, each side of $[a,b]$ has at most one positive fiber with an outside-supporting trace and at most one with an inside-supporting trace. Each such base is an endpoint of the projection of the appropriate closed cut body.
title: A single one-sided buffered cap restricts integer source width
